mn-county-commissioner-roster.summary: Your County Commissioner District card names whoever won the seat at its most recent election, which is not always who holds it today, and two seats name nobody.
mn-county-commissioner-roster.why: The names are election winners from the Secretary of State's results, dated to that election. Nobody publishes a statewide list of who holds each seat now, so a resignation or appointment since is not shown.
mn-county-commissioner-roster.wanted: A statewide list of who holds each seat now, kept up to date, or each county's own board page read on a schedule to catch changes between elections.

mn-county-officers.summary: Your County card names the county and nobody who runs it — no board, no auditor, no sheriff, no attorney.
mn-county-officers.why: Minnesota has no statewide list of county officers. Each county publishes its own, and this app has read none of them yet.
mn-county-officers.wanted: A statewide list of Minnesota's elected county officers, or a per-county page set this app can read on a weekly schedule.

mn-elementary-district-grades.area: Minnesota — eight districts: Browns Valley, Ivanhoe, Lake Benton, Lynd, Milroy, Nett Lake, Pine Point, Round Lake-Brewster
mn-elementary-district-grades.summary: For eight districts the map cannot tell you which grades the district runs, or where its older pupils go.
mn-elementary-district-grades.why: The Census puts these eight in its elementary tiling and then records seven of them as serving every grade anyway. Nothing published here settles the contradiction, so the card states the tiling and claims nothing about the grades.
mn-elementary-district-grades.wanted: The state's own record of which grades each of these eight districts operates, and which district serves their older pupils where they do not.

mn-judicial-roster.summary: Your Judicial District card names the district and how many judgeships it is allowed, and names none of the judges.
mn-judicial-roster.why: The court system publishes its judges, and its website turns away every automated request this project makes, so no name can be carried here without a person reading it off the page.
mn-judicial-roster.wanted: Nothing from a reader. Either the challenge lifts, or a judicial-branch roster turns up somewhere a request can reach.

mn-legislature-roster.summary: Your Minnesota Senate and House cards name the district you are in and nobody who holds it.
mn-legislature-roster.why: The Legislature publishes both rosters and this app has not built them yet. The cards link each chamber's own member directory instead of naming a member it has not verified.
mn-legislature-roster.wanted: Nothing from a reader — this one is ours to build.

mn-municipal-officeholders.summary: In cities under 25,000 people, your City card names the city and nobody who governs it.
mn-municipal-officeholders.why: The 43 larger cities name their mayor and council from the state's election results. The smaller cities are in the same results files and have not been read yet.
mn-municipal-officeholders.wanted: Each smaller city's council size and seat structure, so the results the state already publishes can name its mayor and council.

mn-school-board-members.summary: Your School District card names whoever won each board seat at its most recent election, which is not always who sits on the board today, and some seats name nobody.
mn-school-board-members.why: The names are election winners from the Secretary of State's results, dated to that election. Nobody publishes a statewide list of who sits on each board now, so a resignation or an appointment since is not shown.
mn-school-board-members.wanted: A statewide list of who sits on each school board now, kept up to date, or each district's own board page read on a schedule to catch changes between elections.

mn-township-officers.summary: Your Township card names the township and nobody on its town board.
mn-township-officers.why: A Minnesota town elects three supervisors plus a clerk and a treasurer, and no statewide list pairing each of the 1,797 towns with those officers was found. Each town publishes its own, where it publishes at all.
mn-township-officers.wanted: A statewide list of Minnesota's town supervisors, clerks and treasurers, or a per-town page set this app can read on a schedule.

mn-tribal-government.summary: No card names the tribal nation whose land you clicked on, or its government. Eleven nations hold reservations in Minnesota and a twelfth holds land in trust here, and not one of them appears on any card.
mn-tribal-government.why: Each nation publishes its own council, and its own election districts where it elects by district, on its own site. No state or federal source lists them together, so this app has no roster it could name anyone from.
mn-tribal-government.wanted: Each nation's own published list of its council members, and its district map where it elects by district.
